chunks: From him, from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Ibn Ribat, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I heard your father saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) gave his wives the choice, and they chose Allah and His Messenger, so he did not keep them bound by divorce. And if they had chosen themselves, he would have divorced them.' He (Abu Abdillah) said: 'This is a hadith that my father used to narrate from Aishah. And what is there for the people regarding the choice? This is something Allah specifically granted to His Messenger (peace be upon him).'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the choice given to the Prophet's wives and the general ruling for others?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the 'choice' (Takhayyur) narrated by his father from Aishah was a unique privilege (Khasiyyah) granted exclusively to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his wives, rather than a general legal precedent for all Muslims. He explains that since the Prophet's wives chose Allah and His Messenger, he remained with them without issuing a formal divorce, whereas if they had chosen themselves, he would have divorced them. This distinction highlights the special status of the Prophet's household in Shia jurisprudence, separating their specific rulings from the general rules of marriage and divorce.
